method.name: Pearson's chi-square test of independence
method.evaluates: Whether the distribution of the outcome column's categories differs between groups more than chance would explain.
assumptions: Each row is treated as an independent observation. Paired or repeated measurements of the same subject are not supported.
Expected counts are large enough for the chi-square approximation: none below 1 and no more than 20% below 5.

method.name: Cramér's V
method.evaluates: Strength of association from 0 (none) to 1 (one column determines the other). It does not indicate direction or cause.

association.reason: Column 'country' has only one category in the compared rows, so there is no association to test.

response.note: These results describe how categories co-occur in this dataset. An association does not show that one column causes the other and is not, by itself, evidence of bias.
